body:
CURRENT REMOTE RUNNER AGREEMENT — Engram and TermAl. Current operating guidance, not new execution, Git, installation or restart authority. Superseded assumptions and incident history remain in prior revisions and work notes.

ROUTE
Use the existing authenticated federation/native mailbox to hand a job to an appropriate native root on the runner host; that root uses its own local TermAl test-runs/launcher and returns terminal metadata/completion. Agents submit the exact input and read bounded summaries or necessary failure diagnostics; TermAl owns process, logs and wakes. No stdout following, polling or second transport.
Fable2 reports end-to-end success on 2026-10-31: native mail -> DL560 native root -> LOCAL launcher foreground test-ceeaac7a PASS, and detached test-9fcbdcc9 PASS with cross-host --notify; completion reached Central at07:25:44Z. Source: Fable2 #278/message4cb26c23-d573-4cc6-a46d-9a02a5ba4ee8, TermAl w-c3f102d77999 note2b2442ab. No separate remote SSH command or Central remote-start API was used (the federation transport can still use its SSH tunnel). This is the coordinator's report of route validation, not a new landing-gate verdict or claim that automatic result admission is implemented. Remaining automatic admission belongs to existing K3 w-48c4a207f226; it is separate from launching and returning a run. Central's unsupported remote-start API does not by itself block a native root's LOCAL launcher. Do not add direct-prompt dispatch, executor placement, allocatedSessions, re-pairing or extra onboarding as ordinary native-mail prerequisites.
A directory entry alone does not prove a runnable session; null telemetry does not prove route failure. A send receipt is immutable AT SEND TIME: durableButNotWoken means wake unconfirmed then, even if a wake/reply follows. A suspected current gap uses the existing exact-message current read and target ACK cursor; do not resend or diagnose a reporting defect from the old receipt alone.
The federation's own SSH tunnel is normal transport. A separate agent-operated remote SSH shell is only a named fallback for a concrete missing/broken step. Before falling back for the same job, reconcile whether the original native request already launched or finished; unknown outcomes must not create duplicate runs.

HOSTS AND CAPACITY
CURRENT ENGRAM NATIVE ROOTS (setup readiness confirmed by Opus3 #24-25, 2026-10-31T07:49Z; rediscover after retirement/404):
- DL560 Claude: host:e83d08f4-22ac-4655-a84d-941fc0eeb4f1::session-4, /home/greg/github/Engram-runner.
- Windows B Codex: host:932a546b-4ab2-49a7-a5cb-499cbfac2eab::session-9, F:/GitHub/Personal/Engram-runner; native brief reply and read-only tooling/clean-checkout checks received. About45.55GiB free commit,343.47GiB disk at setup.
- Mac Codex: host:abf8bda6-1ac7-485c-91ce-5a06ac453653::session-6201, /Users/greg/GitHub/Personal/Engram-runner; native brief reply and read-only tooling/clean-checkout checks received. About68.96GiB disk at setup: focused-only until the coordinator assesses full-gate space against the60GB floor.
All three roots replied; setup readiness is complete, not a gate verdict or automatic admission proof. Mac Claude6200 and Windows B Claude8 are limit-paused with queued briefs and stay unused until reset; replacement roots add no host capacity. No job moved during setup. Coordinators retain existing launch/GO ownership. Missing Engram tools/ENGRAM_HOME on an isolated runner is intentional. Dedicated Mac/Windows clones were bootstrapped once with SSH, disclosed to Greg; ongoing jobs use native mail and local test-runs.

DL560 is Engram's preferred runner; the Mac is TermAl's. Either project may use the other's host when its own lane is idle, telling its coordinator first. Windows-only checks stay on Windows.
Engram::Fable schedules Engram lanes on DL560; Termal::Fable2 schedules TermAl lanes, Mac, Windows B and Central. Limits are PER HOST:
- DL560: initially 2 concurrent jobs (1 Engram + 1 TermAl). Raise 2 -> 4 -> further only while measured overlap slowdown versus solo stays about below 20% and RAM below about 70%. Heavy Nmax/repeat-stress alone or with at most one light job.
- Mac M1/16GB: 1 job.
- Windows B/64GB: 1 full gate OR 2 focused jobs, with at least 25GiB free commit at launch.
- Central: 1 Cargo job; quiet for full/whole-bin runs until measured again.
Never infer a new build slot from an idle coding session.

ISOLATION AND INPUT
Use a separate runner clone per project/host, push URL disabled, and a fresh detached worktree per job. Each has its own target and throwaway home under ignored target; no shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR, real ENGRAM_HOME or live store. Unix runner environment: env -i and ulimit -n 16384. Preserve at least 60GB disk free beyond existing reservations. Cleanup follows current repository evidence-retention rules.
DL560 Engram runner clone: ~/github/Engram-runner, never Greg's ~/github/Engram. A filtered test must actually execute at least one named test.
Use the repository's candidate-commit/test-ref or explicitly supported staged-input route. Candidate commits are permitted by current AGENTS; no amend/rebase/force push. A test-ref landing gate counts only under current AGENTS: exact authorized input/tree, standard launcher, required completion input check, platform coverage and integration-owner recording of actual run/host/commit/tree/results. No extra manual hash, recognized-check import or evidence bundle. An ordinary focused remote result is evidence, not a full gate.
The prior Unix diagnostics flock caveat is retired: its fix landed as dcbff8c7. No Central-only gate restriction remains from that defect.
Automatic remote-result admission remains separate from job delivery; unfinished automation is not a prerequisite for native mailbox handoff. Use current repository landing rules and the existing admission owners (TermAl w-c3f102d77999; Engram w-180d6f507470), not historical manual-import rules.

SSH FALLBACK ONLY
Use the configured dl560 SSH alias with BatchMode=yes and StrictHostKeyChecking=yes; do not change global config or invent a remote TERMAL_SESSION_ID. A remote TermAl CLI has the remote host's identity, not the Central operator's.
Where the concrete fallback is required, run the launcher in foreground inside one owned SSH command, never nohup. Preserve the existing completion/backstop safeguard: Claude operators can receive shell-exit wakes; Codex foreground exec has no such guaranteed wake. For a Codex fallback, START names a dedicated backstop T, Fable2 sets its one-shot and confirms SET for T before launch. On the first completion/backstop wake, read summary once and reconcile; never rerun because notification was lost. This fallback safeguard is not a prerequisite added to native TermAl-run jobs.

SOURCES
Current host-cap/isolation agreement: both coordinators #5332-5334; Greg's per-host capacity and test-runs directions are preserved in earlier revisions. Current remote test-ref authority: actual AGENTS and rules-greg-equivalent-gate-hosts-2026-10-28. Current route correction: Architect3 shared-contract notes b49ece40016f49aea61812d5597bb0af, 6560313b36104f96990752e37ea009a4, 1173483468c14779ba9fe614ac9e650b; Fable2 #271-273 and Engram Fable #202-203. Stale remote-full-gates documentation correction belongs to TermAl w-1084790d8a16.

SUPERSEDES the DL560 cap above (Greg direct, 2026-10-31 15:49Z, via Advisor #2459): the one-slot limit is removed. The single shared rule is TermAl memory dl560-parallel-jobs-greg-2026-10-31:
- at most 3 jobs host-wide;
- launch census: MemAvailable ≥ 64 GiB, disk ≥ 100 GB, load < 100;
- CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=48 when 2 or more jobs are running;
- one worktree and target per job, a GO per job, no retry.
